newsitem.title: USA: Matria to cut staff, CEO to step down.
newsitem.headline: Matria to cut staff, CEO to step down.

text.p: Matria Healthcare Inc. said Tuesday that Robert Byrnes will step down as president and chief executive at the end of the year, and more jobs will be cut at the health care company in a restructuring.

The restructuring follows the March merger of Tokos Medical Corp. and Healthdyne Maternity Management to form Matria, which provides obstetrical home care and maternity management services to health management organisations.
Matria said it would cut more field and corporate staff by the end of the year as a final step in its merger consolidation.
These and other restructuring steps will result in a charge of about $7.5 million in the fourth quarter, and reduce Matria's annual operating expenses by about $5 million per year, the company said.

Matria also said it was forming a search committee to find find a new chief executive as soon as possible. Until a successor was named, Chairman Parker Petit and Donald Millard, senior vice president of finance, would jointly act as company president.

Byrnes had been the chairman and chief executive officer of Tokos, and became president and chief executive of Matria after the merger, the company said. Marietta, Ga.-based Matria's stock fell 62.50 cents to $5.50 on Nasdaq in late trading.
